subject.title: Feature: fire session-memory hook on session reset/prune, not just compaction

question: Should OpenClaw expose one unified pre-finalization lifecycle for manual reset, automatic daily/idle rollover, and maintenance prune, or keep daily/idle/prune on separate hook surfaces?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API affects plugin-visible hook semantics, transcript retention, async lifecycle timing, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose it alone.

options.title: Define unified pre-finalization lifecycle
options.body: Create a single maintainer-approved lifecycle contract that covers reset, automatic rollover, and destructive prune before wiring session-memory to it.

options.title: Land reset-only path first
options.body: Accept the active daily/idle reset candidate as a partial fix while keeping this issue open for prune and lifecycle finalization design.

options.title: Keep behavior plugin-specific
options.body: Decline core lifecycle expansion for now and document external snapshot or plugin-specific workarounds instead.

recommendation.title: Define unified pre-finalization lifecycle
recommendation.body: Create a single maintainer-approved lifecycle contract that covers reset, automatic rollover, and destructive prune before wiring session-memory to it.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is tied to the active reset candidate, adjacent prune lifecycle PR, and recent hook/session-memory work.
